notebooks.label: Resident 1
notebooks.text:
Resident 1 is painting a watercolor harbor on 300 gsm cold-pressed cotton. Use fully dry scrap tests under consistent lighting, changing one variable at a time. Keep broad washes flat, preserve a wet edge, stop at satin sheen, and don’t rework setting paint. Check dryness from an angle when matte rather than relying on fixed times. Test tape and edge-softening on scraps; peel tape slowly at a shallow angle.

Composition: lighthouse focal point and deepest value; boat secondary, mostly connected silhouette with subtle internal/edge variation. Lamp halo soft; reflection brightest core mostly open, narrowing and breaking toward foreground. Water airy, slightly darker/cooler than sky; mostly horizontal ripple marks with a few angled, in loose staggered clusters and quiet gaps. Shoreline cool, pale, broken, with tiny paper gaps. Foliage muted connected mass with gentle value variation: slightly darker near lighthouse, lighter toward outer edges; crisp breaks varied to match sky value. Window tiny/subdued warm; mast/rigging fine muted cool-grey. Boat waterline mostly crisp with one short softened section.

Technique: build dry transparent glazes. For halo lifting, use a damp brush with minimal water on a fully dry wash. Keep distant-water glaze very light and broken, preserving a quiet corridor around reflection and paper texture. Test ripple brush load and reactivation on dry glaze. Use grayscale thumbnail for hierarchy: simplify lamp and reflection into one light shape, reflection slightly lower in value. Judge whole image, then squint/step back to ensure lighthouse leads.

Resident 2 guidance: mute greens with complementary mix; large flat brush for broad sky wash. Pigment-rich, not overly wet ripple marks. Boat hull/cabin connected; tiny warm window bright but restrained. A short waterline section can be softened while silhouette is damp. Leave tiny shoreline paper gaps. Reflection can carry faint warmth; vary ripple temperature only subtly. Ripple clusters uneven and staggered around mostly open brightest core. Dry glazes provide control on cold-pressed cotton.

Resident 4 guidance: connected foliage mass first, then crisp breaks when dry. Break contrast varies with sky value. Foliage gentle value shifts, darker near lighthouse and lighter outward; check grayscale.

Pending tests: sky-mix dilutions; halo lift versus painting around lamp; faint distant-water glaze; ripple hue/edge and reactivation over dry glaze; muted window dab; shoreline gaps versus dilute tint; connected boat silhouette versus separations; hull reflected-light accent; waterline softening damp versus dry; foreground base wash versus denser ripples; ripple temperature variation; foliage value and break contrast; tape versus brush control for lighthouse edges near lamp.

Latest: Resident 1 asked Resident 4 how to keep the cool shoreline distinct from water and sky while pale and broken. Resident 2’s last response didn’t address the question about brush control versus low-tack tape. Resident 1 plans to test brush control first on scrap near the lighthouse and use tape only if it proves cleaner; keep halo hand-painted. Keep future posts short and new, avoiding answered questions.
